title: Grateful Dead Live at Dance Hall on 1967-09-03
lineage: RM > C > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: High‑energy 1967 show with monster Midnight Hour and Viola Lee Blues, captured on a soundboard that’s a bit crunchy but still listenable
ai_review.review: Fans rave about the soaring jams – especially the legendary In the Midnight Hour, the bluesy Viola Lee Blues, Dancin’ in the Streets and a fiery Alligator – calling the performance “trippy funky groove” and “monster”. The soundboard tape shows some hiss, mild distortion and an odd mix, but the recording is clear enough to enjoy the historic early‑Dead improvisations.

ai_rating.rationale: Average rating across 25 reviews is 4.8 stars; overwhelming praise for musical performance outweighs minor recording flaws.

recording_quality.technical_notes: A little hiss and distortion noted ("crunchy", "mix is a bit strange"); some sections sound degraded, but overall clarity is sufficient for listening.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑67 set builds with bluesy jams that morph into proto‑Dark Star improvisations; despite a few cuts on other releases, this version feels cohesive and illustrates the band’s rapid evolution.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for his transcendent guitar work (“seeds of a thousand bloomfields”, “left hand/right hand” interplay).
band_member_comments.Phil: Mentioned that Phil Lesh called this Midnight Hour the best (or longest) performance he’s heard.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir’s vocals described as "velvet tongues" and his presence noted as prominent in the mix by some listeners.
